strengths_deep_dive: HRD demonstrates financial efficiency by directing an <cite id="5">81.6% program expense ratio</cite> toward direct service programs in conflict zones in FY2024 [5]. This efficiency is paired with low fundraising costs, spending only <cite id="1">$0.06 to raise every $1</cite> [1]. Evaluators highlight HRD's operational stability, backed by an <cite id="1">overall rating of 97.3/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> and a Candid Platinum Seal [1]. Furthermore, HRD maintains <cite id="1">15.0 months of working capital</cite>, securing long-term programmatic commitments even during economic fluctuations [1].
rich_narrative.summary: Humanity for Relief and Development (HRD) operates as an international humanitarian nonprofit focusing primarily on direct emergency aid and food security in Yemen [4, 5]. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="5">$3,669,260 in total revenue</cite> to provide essential nutritional support through targeted initiatives like Mercy Bakery, Mercy Kitchen, and specialized nutrition programs for cancer patients [5]. HRD maintains a strong financial standing with a <cite id="1">97.3/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by robust operational discipline [1]. The organization allocates <cite id="5">78.1% of its expenses to programs</cite>, beating the 75% industry standard benchmark while maintaining low overhead [5]. While HRD demonstrates high directness in program execution, its overall board size of four members presents an area where governance structures could be expanded as the institution matures [5]. Donations to HRD qualify as zakat-eligible, serving specified categories including the poor and needy [4].
